header: WHAT AN ERROR RECORD MAY CONTAIN (22 Nov 2026). An error message is written by code, but it can carry what the code was holding: an e-mail address, a ticket number, a phone number, a database's "Key (name)=(...) already exists", a token in a link. Nothing like that is kept or sent anywhere: I mask it HERE, before the record is stored, grouped, shown to the developer or put in a notice. The text for the AI model is masked further (maskForModel): the manual promises that names never go to the model, so quoted words that could be a name are hidden too, and only code locations of the stack are sent. Pure functions.

symbols.name: scrubText
symbols.sig: export function scrubText(text: unknown, max = 2000): string
doc: Returns the text with e-mail addresses, numbers that identify a person, link queries, tokens and "Key (x)=(value)" details masked.

symbols.name: pathOnly
doc: Returns a path with no query string and no fragment, at most 200 characters ("/search?q=goutam" becomes "/search").

symbols.name: maskForModel
doc: I hide quoted words that could be a name, a value or a sentence; a plain identifier ('map', 'pg-pool', './x') stays, because it is what makes an error readable.

symbols.name: stackFrames
symbols.sig: export function stackFrames(stack: unknown, n = 5): string[]
doc: Returns the code locations of a stack, without line numbers, hashes or the machine's folders: "at fn (app/api/x/route.js)". At most `n` frames.

symbols.name: fingerprintSource
symbols.sig: export function fingerprintSource(source: string, message: string, stack?: string): string
doc: This is what makes two records "the same error": I use the message without its numbers and quoted values, and the first code location. The caller hashes it.
